| [CASE-203](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-203.md) | The U.S. fire incident reporting guidance on cancelled dispatches, 2023: units assigned, arrived and turned back are recorded, while a call a department could not answer for lack of resources is not an incident at all, so the data omit the failures that most concern readiness | Filed at the owner's request on 2026-11-04, to account for what the reading of the U.S. Fire Administration's NFIRS coding guidance ([LIT-2084](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2084.md), read in [NOTE-1573](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1573.md)) surfaced and the record lacked. The National Fire Incident Reporting System records, for each incident, every unit assigned, whether it arrived, and whether it was cancelled en route; but a call the department knew of and could not answer for lack of resources is not an NFIRS incident, and recording it in a separate database is recommended, not required. The wording is the filer's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
